walkthroughs.body_html:
Kinematics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Kinematics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Kinematics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²
5.33, by dividing 80 by 15.
15, because 15% means 15 units out of any amount.
Expressions are easier versions of equations.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the expression 3x + 5 and the equation 3x + 5 = 11?
options: Expressions and equations are the same — you can solve either one.
An expression has no equals sign and cannot be solved; an equation states two things are equal and can be solved for x.
5.33, by dividing 80 by 15.
Expressions are easier versions of equations.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vertical motion under gravity”?
options: Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variable acceleration”?
options: If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “SUVAT equations”?
options: Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
